Corporate Mitra Scheme Awareness Webinar organized by IICA Shillong, Ministry of Corporate Affairs witnessing overwhelming participation of youth and enterprises of Mizoram
articles.full_content:
The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, successfully organised a webinar on 27 July 2026, for awareness and sensitisation of the Corporate Mitra Scheme for the youth, students, MSMEs, professionals and enterprises of Mizoram.
The webinar for Mizoram was conducted as part of the Scheme’s Awareness Campaign, for the Northeast Region (NER). Mizoram University, Aizawl , facilitated the program, with mass outreach and participant mobilization for the event in the state, and The Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI) supported - as the “lead co-host”; with The Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) and The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) – supporting as the “support co-host”.
The Corporate Mitra Scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 with the aim to empower MSMEs, primarily in the Tier-3 & 2 cities, by facilitating the MSMEs in playing their part in the larger vision of a Viksit Bharat @ 2047.
The initiative embodies the vision of a formalized, financially sustainable, and a thriving MSME sector, by creating a strong support ecosystem for the MSMEs, by providing access to a pool of qualified, accredited and trusted para professionals – called the “Corporate Mitras”. The initiative aims to create a cadre of business support para-professionals, by equipping young graduates with industry-relevant knowledge and practical skills and making them industry ready to provide accessible, affordable, and quality compliance, assistance and business support services to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
The accredited Corporate Mitra(s) shall provide professional assistance to the local enterprises, for the non-core aspects of their business operation i.e. regulatory, compliance, financial, taxation, accounting, and governance-related needs, thereby ensuring that MSMEs can focus on innovation, expansion and growth, while meeting regulatory requirements with ease.
For Scheme’s rollout and implementation for the Northeast region, Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA)-Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs has been designated as the nodal agency for coordination and liaison with State Governments and other stakeholders (universities/associations/industry bodies/institutes etc.), for promotion, and awareness of the Scheme.
Registration for the 'Corporate Mitra' Course was launched on 15th July 2026 and shall be live up till to 31st July 2026 (Registration Link: https://swayamplus.education.gov.in/courses/corporate-mitra ).
The webinar commenced with the welcome address and context-setting by Sh. Debarun Kalita, Officer on Special Duty (OSD) for IICA Shillong , also the designated Nodal Officer for the Corporate Mitra Scheme for the Northeast. Sh. Kalita, at the outset expressed his deep gratitude to the visionary leadership of the Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs for her strategic guidance in developing the Corporate Mitra conce
articles.summary: The Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), Shillong, under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, successfully organised a webinar on 27 July 2026, for awareness and sensitisation of the Corporate Mitra Scheme for the youth, students, MSMEs, professionals and enterprises of Mizoram. The webinar for Mizoram was conducted as part of the Scheme’s Awareness Campaign, for the Northeast Region (NER). Mizoram University, Aizawl , facilitated the program, with mass outreach and participant mobilization for the event in the state, and The Institute of Cost Accountants of India (ICMAI) supported - as the “lead co-host”; with The Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) and The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI) – supporting as the “support co-host”.

Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) revised base year of the Consumer Price Index from 2012=100 to 2024=100
articles.full_content:
Monthly price collection under new CPI series has been extended to 1465 rural markets and 1395 urban markets across 434 towns
The Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) revised the base year of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from 2012=100 to 2024=100. The revised series was released on 12 th February, 2026. The monthly price collection under the new CPI series has been extended to 1465 rural markets and 1395 urban markets across 434 towns. In addition, 12 online markets have been added across 12 towns, having population of more than 25 lakh each, to capture price variations of items on e-commerce/online platforms. The total number of weighted items in the revised basket at All India level has been increased from 299 to 358, with goods increasing from 259 to 308 and services from 40 to 50. The item basket and weights of the new series are based on the results of the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2023-24.
Under the CPI 2024 series, the inflation data is available from January, 2026 onwards. The inflation data of the CPI 2012 series is available up to December, 2025. A direct comparison of inflation under the new series with that of the previous series is not feasible on account of the changes in the item basket, weights, coverage of markets and methodology between the two series.
The month-wise inflation under the new series since January, 2026, however, is as follows:
Inflation (year on year) under CPI 2024 series
To communicate the State Governments, financial institutions, experts, academicians and other users on the changes in the revised series vis-à-vis old series, the Expert Group Report on Comprehensive Updation of Consumer Price Index, containing the details of the revised methodology and practices adopted in the new series, was released on 29 th January, 2026, prior to the release of the first index of the new series for better understanding and assimilation of the new CPI series. Thereafter, MoSPI, through press conference, brainstorming sessions, panel discussions, media articles etc. sensitized users on the revised series.
In order to establish the time series and continuity between the CPI (Base: 2012=100) and CPI (Base: 2024=100) series, linking factors and its method of calculation were also released. Further, back series data of the All India General Indices and inflation for the Rural, Urban and Combined sectors for the period from January 2013 to December 2024 is also available at e-Sankhyiki Portal of MoSPI (www.esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in).
This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of
Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Lok Sabha today.
articles.summary: Monthly price collection under new CPI series has been extended to 1465 rural markets and 1395 urban markets across 434 towns The Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation (MoSPI) revised the base year of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from 2012=100 to 2024=100. The revised series was released on 12 th February, 2026. The monthly price collection under the new CPI series has been extended to 1465 rural markets and 1395 urban markets across 434 towns.

PIB Imphal Hosts Varta on PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana in Thoubal
articles.full_content:
Additional Director General Urges Media Support for Viksit Bharat@2047; 1,557 Rooftop Solar Installations Completed in Manipur
The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Regional Office, Imphal, organised a one-day media workshop (Varta) on PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana at Kshetri Shanglen, Thoubal, on Tuesday. The workshop formed part of PIB’s outreach initiative highlighting the achievements of the Government of India over the past 12 years and aimed to equip journalists with comprehensive knowledge of the flagship rooftop solar scheme.
The programme was organised to enable media professionals to effectively disseminate information on the scheme’s objectives, provisions, and benefits, thereby enhancing public awareness and encouraging wider participation.
The inaugural session was attended by Dr. Engam Pame, IIS, Additional Director General, PIB, RO Imphal; Sh. Niti Devi, General Manager (RE), MSPDCL; Nongthombam Purnima Devi, Manager (Electrical), MSPDCL; Moirangthem Rustum Singh, Assistant Director, Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Field Office Chandel; and Pushpa Maibam, Media and Communication Officer, PIB, RO Imphal.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Engam Pame underscored the crucial role of the media in connecting citizens with government welfare and development programmes.
Calling journalists “agents of change,” he urged them to actively support the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047, stressing that informed and responsible journalism is essential for ensuring that government initiatives reach every eligible beneficiary.
“The media has a vital responsibility in creating awareness and empowering citizens with accurate information. Let us work together to realise the vision of a developed India,” he said.
He observed that despite significant progress since Independence, many citizens continue to face socio-economic challenges. To address these, the Government of India has adopted a people-centric development model focused on delivering essential services—including safe drinking water, healthcare, sanitation, LPG connections, education, and financial assistance—directly to households.
Reiterating that the success of Viksit Bharat@2047 depends on collective public participation, Dr. Pame said the PIB remains committed to strengthening communication between the government and citizens through the media.
Speaking on the occasion, Sh. Niti Devi, General Manager (RE), MSPDCL, said workshops of this nature play a significant role in enhancing public awareness of the scheme. She described PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana as a transformative initiative that promotes clean energy adoption while reducing dependence on conventional thermal power generation.
She noted that rooftop solar installations not only help reduce electricity bills but also contribute to environmental sustainability by lowering carbon emissions.
Launched on 15 February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore, the scheme aims to provide up to 300 units of free electricity per month to elig

articles.full_content:
Electronics Production Grows Seven-Fold to Over ₹13 Lakh Crore, Exports Increase Eleven-Fold to Over ₹4 Lakh Crore in the Last 12 Years Electronics Manufacturing Ecosystem Supports Around 25 Lakh Jobs, with Mobile Manufacturing Employing Around 12 Lakh People and Women Constituting Nearly 70% of Workforce in High-Precision Manufacturing Segments
Driven by Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, Government of India has taken several policy initiatives to develop a complete ecosystem of electronics manufacturing.
The Government adopted a well thought out strategy to develop India’s electronic manufacturing ecosystem - beginning with the manufacturing of finished products, followed by sub-assemblies, components, and eventually machinery and tools. At the same time, the Government focused on creating the necessary infrastructure to support electronics manufacturing.
As a result of these initiatives, India has emerged as a global electronics manufacturing hub. Electronic manufacture in India has expanded significantly in the last 12 years, which can be seen from the following statistics:
Production of electronics goods (₹)
Increased 7 times
Export of electronics goods (₹)
Increased 11 times
Production of mobile phones (₹)
Increased 33 times
Export of mobile phones (₹)
Increased 165 times
The electronics production has increased from Rs. 11.32 lakh crores in FY 2024-25 to Rs. 13.11 Lakh crores in FY 2025-26 growing at a year-on-year growth rate of 15.8% in the last one year.
The growth in electronics manufacturing has been possible due to various measures taken by the Government in the last 12 years to promote domestic production, exports and value addition of electronic goods including mobile phones, IT Hardware and electronic components. Some of the major initiatives include:
• PLI Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing
• PLI Scheme 2.0 for IT Hardware
• Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS)
• Semicon India Programme
• Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC 2.0) Scheme
• Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)
• Modified Programme for Development of Semiconductors and Display Manufacturing Ecosystem in India.
• Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order to promote using made in India goods.
• Allowing 100% FDI in the sector
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM)
The Government of India launched the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Large Scale Electronics Manufacturing (LSEM) in 2020 to boost domestic manufacturing of mobile phones in the country.

NSO Guwahati Organises Workshop on Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises (ASISSE)-2026
articles.full_content:
The National Statistics Office (NSO), Regional Office, Guwahati, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, organised a workshop on the Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises (ASISSE)-2026 on July 29, 2026 at Guwahati. The workshop was attended by senior officers of NSO (Field Operations Division) and representatives of various service sector units from Assam.
On this occasion Shri N. Mohondas Singh, Director and Regional Head, NSO Regional Office, Guwahati appreciated the enthusiastic participation of the stakeholders and highlighted the significance of the survey . He informed that the workshop had been organised to sensitise enterprise units and equip them with the necessary knowledge for self-compilation of survey returns, thereby ensuring timely and accurate submission of data.
The technical sessions conducted included detailed presentations on survey schedules, reporting procedures, and a live demonstration of the ASISSE web portal, followed by hands-on training to familiarise participants with the online data submission process.
The service sector plays a crucial role in the Indian economy and has become India’s most powerful growth engine in the past few decades. The contribution of service sector is maximum in the country’s GDP. While unincorporated service sector is covered in the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) conducted by National Statistics Office (NSO), regular data pertaining to detailed economic and operational characteristics, employment, etc. are not available with industry-wise or State/UT-wise break-up for the incorporated service sector. To address this data gap, it was felt necessary to build a comprehensive database of corporate service sector enterprises with the desired level of granularity through a regular annual survey. This prompted NSO to launch a new survey dedicated to the sector.
The principal objective of Annual Survey of Incorporated Services Sector Enterprises (ASISSE) is to develop a comprehensive database of the corporate service sector of the country. Given the importance of this sector, it is imperative that a survey may be designed to capture the key characteristics such as gross value added (GVA), fixed capital, capital formation, employment, emoluments paid and other important features pertaining to the units belonging to the sector not only at State level but also at different industry level.
The coverage of ASISSE is essentially the corporate entities i.e. entities registered under Companies Act, 1956 or Companies Act, 2013 or Limited Liability Partnership (LLP) Act, 2008 and belonging to service sector. Unincorporated entities are excluded from coverage of ASISSE.
The reference period for ASISSE-2026 is the financial year 2024-25, covering the period from April 2024 to March 2025. The survey has a sample size of approximately 1.25 lakh enterprises across the country. Field operations commenced in April 2026
articles.summary: The National Statistics Office (NSO), Regional Office, Guwahati, under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, organised a workshop on the Annual Survey of Incorporated Service Sector Enterprises (ASISSE)-2026 on July 29, 2026 at Guwahati. The workshop was attended by senior officers of NSO (Field Operations Division) and representatives of various service sector units from Assam. Mohondas Singh, Director and Regional Head, NSO Regional Office, Guwahati appreciated the enthusiastic participation of the stakeholders and highlighted the significance of the survey .

articles.full_content:
The CSIR–Institute of Minerals & Materials Technology (CSIR-IMMT), Bhubaneswar, inaugurated its Advanced E-Learning Centre under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative on 27 th July 2026 (Monday), marking a significant milestone in promoting digital learning, capacity building and skill development.
The programme commenced with a tree plantation drive led by Dr. Vinay Kumar, Scientist-G and Nodal Scientist, CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, CSIR-Human Resource Development Centre (CSIR-HRDC) . The Advanced E-Learning Centre was formally inaugurated by Dr. Vinay Kumar in the presence of Dr. Ramanuj Narayan, Director, CSIR-IMMT .
The inaugural ceremony was followed by a Skill Development Meeting at S S Bhatnagar Hall , attended by scientists, research scholars, students and staff of the institute.
Welcoming the gathering, Dr. Ramanuj Narayan , Director, CSIR-IMMT, highlighted the institute's commitment to strengthening digital education, innovation and skill development through modern learning infrastructure. He emphasized that the newly established centre would play an important role in expanding access to quality learning resources and enhancing the professional competencies of students, researchers and industry personnel.
Dr. Santosh Kumar Behera, Scientist-F and Skill Development Coordinator, CSIR-IMMT , presented an overview of the institute's skill development initiatives under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative. He highlighted the successful implementation of various training programmes, industry-oriented courses and capacity-building activities that have benefited students, professionals and researchers from across the country.
Addressing the gathering, Dr. Trupti Das, Scientist-G, Chief Scientist and Chairperson (HRD), CSIR-IMMT , stressed the importance of continuous learning, human resource development and technology-enabled education in preparing a skilled workforce for emerging industrial and research challenges.
Dr. L. D. Besra, Scientist-G and Head, CSIR-IMMT, highlighted the importance of skill development programmes in enhancing employability, fostering innovation and bridging the gap between academic learning and industry requirements. He emphasized that continuous skill upgradation is essential for building a competent and future-ready workforce
Delivering the keynote address, Dr. Vinay Kumar underscored the vision of the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative in creating a nationwide ecosystem for technology-enabled education, digital learning and industry-relevant skill development. He appreciated the efforts of CSIR-IMMT in establishing the Advanced E-Learning Centre and expressed confidence that it would serve as an important platform for online training, hybrid learning programmes, webinars, workshops and collaborative knowledge-sharing activities. The formal vote of thanks was delivered by Dr. Manish Kumar , Scientist-F.

articles.title: Centre Promotes Convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Schemes to Accelerate Solar Adoption and Rural Energy Self-Sufficiency
articles.full_content:
Government has been promoting convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana with suitable Central and State programmes and funding sources, wherever feasible, to facilitate wider adoption of the schemes. For instance, PM KUSUM scheme guidelines allow for convergence with other central schemes including:
• Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme for access of easy financing
• Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) for solarization of segregated agriculture feeders
• Promotion of micro irrigation techniques and Per Drop More Crop scheme
• Replacement of agriculture pumps with energy efficient pumps
• Gram Urja Swaraj Campaign to enhance self-sufficiency at village level
Similarly for PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, the convergence is taken up with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), for implementing the Solar Didi Programme under which women Self-Help Group (SHG) members under DAY-NULM are trained. Convergence of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) funds is also encouraged with PM Surya Ghar for eligible beneficiaries, particularly BPL households, PMAY beneficiaries and other vulnerable sections.
The Ministry has already issued communications and possible areas of convergence to all the states for convergence of PM KUSUM and PMSG Schemes with scheme of Ministry of Cooperation, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development etc.
This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

articles.title: Over 48 Lakh Households Benefit Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Since February 2024
articles.full_content:
The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) is a demand-driven scheme wherein all residential consumers in the country including the rural households, having a grid-connected electricity connection with the local DISCOM, can avail the benefits of the scheme, for installation of rooftop solar (RTS) systems by applying on the National Portal ( www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in ) of the scheme.
During the year 2025-26, a total of 18. 71 lakh RTS systems have been installed with a cumulative installed solar capacity of 6.7 GW, benefitting 22.71 lakh households across the country, including the rural households under the PMSG: MBY.
Under the PMSG: MBY, since its launch in February 2024, a total of 39,72,447 RTS systems have been installed, benefitting 48,02,717 households across the country including the households in rural areas, as on 22.07.2026.
While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 lakh beneficiaries have been reported by DISCOMs across the country , including the rural households to receive zero electricity bill after installation of RTS systems under the scheme during the any month/billing period , depending on their self-consumption of electricity.
Apart from installation of rooftop solar plants in residential sector, the PMSG: MBY also envisage installation of RTS plants in Government and commercial buildings including educational and health institutions, however, no central financial assistance (CFA) is provided to these categories of consumers as installation of rooftop solar plants is financially viable for them even without CFA.
This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

articles.full_content:
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles is being implemented by the Ministry of Textiles across the country to promote the production of MMF Apparel, MMF Fabrics and products of Technical Textiles. The Scheme is aimed at promoting investment, enhancing manufacturing capacities, improving competitiveness of the textile sector and encouraging value addition in the identified product segments. The implementation of the Scheme is monitored and reviewed periodically at various levels in the Ministry. Further, weekly Open House sessions and monthly workshops are organized with the beneficiary companies to facilitate implementation of the Scheme and to resolve issues, if any, relating to project execution. The Ministry also organizes outreach-cum-knowledge sessions in various States, including Maharashtra, to create awareness about the Scheme and facilitate stakeholder participation.
Under the Production Linked Incentive scheme (PLI) for Textiles, a total of 170 companies have been approved across India of which 24 companies pertain to Maharashtra. As of March 31, 2026, investment to the tune of ₹167.51 crores have been made by these companies in Maharashtra. District-wise details are given below.
To make the PLI Scheme more attractive for the prospective investors in the MMF and Technical Textiles sector, the Scheme has been modified in October, 2025, with key revisions such as Expansion of Eligible Notified Products by addition of 17 new HSN codes in MMF Apparel and Fabrics, Relaxation from setting up new companies to avail benefit of the Scheme, Reduction in minimum threshold criteria of investment by 50% and Reduction in incremental turnover Criteria for incentive from earlier 25% to 10%. To create comprehensive awareness and participation, the Ministry has proactively engaged with all major textile industry associations to disseminate information regarding the recent revisions in the Scheme and had also reopened the application portal of the Scheme till 31.03.2026 to accept new applications. As a result of this revision, MSME participation has increased significantly with 65 of the 96 applications received under Round 3 of the Scheme (approximately 68%) pertaining to the MSME sector.

articles.full_content:
Toy Biz International 2026 Showcases 400 Indian Brands, Boosting Domestic Sales and Export Opportunities Government Initiatives Boost Quality, Safety and Competitiveness of India's Toy Industry
The 17th Toy Biz International B2B Exhibition was organized by the Toy Association of India from 4th to 7th July, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Exhibition aimed at promoting Indian toys, facilitating business networking, and creating opportunities for growth in domestic sales and exports. It witnessed participation of 400 Indian toy brands, 100 international buyers from 40 countries, and around 30,000 business visitors. The exhibition provided platform for connecting manufacturers with wholesalers, retailers, distributors, institutional buyers and e-commerce platforms.
At present, there is no dedicated toy policy of the Government of India.
In 2018-19, Toys worth USD 371.7 Mn were imported into India. A large proportion of these toys were unsafe, substandard, counterfeit, and cheap. Further, a Mystery Shopping exercise conducted in 2019 revealed that only 33% toys in the domestic market were of acceptable quality as per BIS standards.
In order to improve the quality and safety of toys in the country and to promote the overall development of the Indian toy industry, the Government of India has undertaken several initiatives. The key initiatives are as follows:
• Formulation of a comprehensive National Action Plan for Toys (NAPT), comprising 21 action points and coordinated by 14 Ministries and Departments. It focuses on promoting the design and development of toys based on Indian values, culture, and history; encouraging the use of toys as learning resources; organizing hackathons, toy fairs, and grand challenges for toy design and manufacturing; strengthening quality monitoring and restricting the import of substandard and unsafe toys; promoting indigenous toy clusters; and boosting domestic manufacturing.
• Basic Custom Duty (BCD) on Toys (HS Code-9503) was increased from 20% to 60% in February 2020, and subsequently increased to 70% in 2023. Further, the BCD on Parts of Electronic Toys (HS 95030091) revised as 20% in the Budget F.Y. 2025-26.
• A Quality Control Order (QCO) for Toys was issued on 25.02.2020, implemented with effect from 01.01.2021.
• BIS has granted more than 1800 licenses to domestic manufacturers of toys and more than 50 licenses to foreign manufacturers for use of BIS Standard Mark on toys conforming to the Indian Standards for safety of toys.
• The National Education Policy 2020 formulated by Ministry of Education focuses on play and activity-based learning. A handbook on ‘Toy Based Pedagogy’ has been published by NCERT with the objective of ensuring that the learning process for children is enjoyable and fun. It prescribes toys, especially based on indigenous toys and games to be used at different stages to help develop many competencies in young children.
• Cluster-based approach adopted to support domestic Toy industry. T

articles.full_content:
Quick Estimates of Index of Industrial Production and Use- Based Index for the Month of June 2026 (Base 2022-23=100)
In June 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded a 7.3% year-on-year growth, supported by 7.8% growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of 10.6% in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.
The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28 th of every month (or next working day if 28 th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.
2. Key Highlights:
• The IIP growth rate for the month of June 2026 is 7.3 percent which was 5.1 percent (Quick Estimate) in the month of May 2026.
• The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 are 1.0 percent, 7.8 percent, 10.6 percent and 6.1 percent respectively.
• The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 123.1 against 114.7 in June 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 stand at 110.0, 123.3, 131.0 and 145.7 respectively.
• Within the Manufacturing sector, 19 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in June 2026 over June 2025. The top three positive contributors for the month of June 2026 are – “Manufacture of electrical equipment” (34.0%), “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” (17.5%), and “Manufacture of food products” (10.8%).
• In the industry group “Manufacture of electrical equipment” item groups “Electrical Apparatus for Switching or Protecting Electrical Circuits (e.g., Switchgear, Circuit Breakers/Switches, Control/Meter Panels) and Parts Thereof”, “UPS and Solid-State Drives”, and “End-Face Connectors for Optical Fibres and Cables” have shown significant contribution in growth.
• In the industry group “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers”, item groups “Auto Components, Spares and Accessories”, “Passenger Cars”, and “Commercial Vehicles” have shown significant contribution in growth.
• In the industry group “Manufacture of food products”, item groups “Tea”, “Rice (Other Than Basmati)”, and “Starch, All Types” have shown significant contribution in growth.

Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 119.8 and 115.4 respectively.

articles.full_content:
The following schemes are administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) to promote domestic manufacturing and technological upgradation:
(i) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government approved this scheme on 23.09.2021 for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products with a budgetary outlay of Rs. 25,938 crore. The scheme provides financial incentives on manufacturing of AAT products including EVs with minimum 50% Domestic Value Addition (DVA) and attract investments in the automotive manufacturing value chain. The Scheme has attracted an investment of Rs. 44,326 Crore and generated employment of 67,820 till 31.03.2026. Further, under the Scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development (R&D) are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects.
(ii) Production Linked Incentive Scheme on National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage: The Government on 12.05.2021 approved PLI Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of Rs.18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries, out of which 40 GWh ACC capacity has been awarded to four beneficiary firms. Under the Scheme, a Giga-Scale ACC manufacturing plant with an installed capacity of 1.4 GWh has been established. The scheme has attracted an investment of ₹5,180 crore and direct employment of 1,277 till 31.05.2026. Further, under the Scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development (R&D) are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects.
(iii) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme: This scheme has been approved with an outlay of Rs. 10,900 crore w.e.f. 01.04.2024 till 31.03.2028. The scheme supports domestic manufacturing of electric vehicles including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. The scheme also supports EV public charging stations and upgradation of testing agencies.
(iv) Scheme on Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector- Phase-II: This Scheme has the objective to encourage technology development and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities. Media serves as the bridge between the Government and Public: Ramanathapuram District Collector Shri M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran
articles.full_content:
The vision of a drug free Tamil Nadu can be achieved only through awareness: Superintendent of Police, Ramananathapuram District
Shri M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran, District Collector, Ramanathapuram, said that Media plays a major role in taking the government welfare measures to the beneficiaries. He said this while presiding over an orientation program for journalists, organized by the Press Information Bureau, Chennai at Ramanathapuram today. The programme aimed at strengthening responsible journalism, enhancing awareness on government initiatives and equipping media professionals with the knowledge to effectively counter misinformation in the digital age.
Speaking at the event, Shri Sivaguru Prabhakaran described the media as the fourth pillar of democracy and appreciated its constructive role in governance. He said several district administration initiatives had been strengthened through proactive media support. Such orientation programmes, help journalists upgrade their knowledge and professional skills.
Shri G. Chandeesh, Superintendent of Police, Ramanathapuram, enlightened the journalists on the importance of effective communication and highlighted the crucial role of the media in ensuring accurate dissemination of information relating to police and government initiatives. Reiterating the vision of a Drug-Free Tamil Nadu, he emphasised that awareness among the public, especially parents and youth, is essential to eliminate drug abuse.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri V. Palanichamy, Director General (i/c) South Zone, Press Information Bureau, underscored the importance of accuracy, brevity and clarity in journalism. He said the media today faces two major challenges—AI-generated content and fake news and the rapid evolution of technology. He urged journalists to uphold professional ethics while embracing technological advancements. He also called upon the media to provide greater coverage to government welfare and developmental initiatives so that their benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.
In a special session, Shri P. Arun Kumar, Director, Press Information Bureau, Chennai, delivered an interactive presentation on misinformation and disinformation. He explained practical methods of verifying digital content, identifying manipulated information and using fact-checking tools to ensure responsible journalism.
During the technical session on Sustainable Fisheries and Blue Economy, Dr. Vikas P.A., Senior Scientist, ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), Mandapam, Ramanathapuram highlighted the vast potential of seaweed cultivation and cage fish farming in improving the livelihoods of coastal communities. He spoke about the Government's continued support for fisheries research and sustainable aquaculture and outlined various initiatives under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), including a Central Government contribution of Rs.9,407 crore for fisheries development.
